response.markdown_report:
## Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Training margins measure local separation. Training-prefix perturbations likewise measure in-sample reliance, since freezing weights does not remove target exposure. (2) Zero padding embeddings do not guarantee invariant GRU states. Verify recurrent masking and final-nonpadding readout before interpretation. (3) Feedback motivates investigating immediate relevance and possible redundancy. Histories and descriptions support proxies; ownership, compatibility and mood remain unknown without evidence.

**Related-work insights.** (1) Betello et al. motivate position-specific perturbations [1]. Their training interventions differ from frozen-model edits. (2) *Does It Look Sequential?* motivates shuffle controls [2]. Preserving the final item separates earlier-order sensitivity from immediate recency dependence. (3) Krichene and Rendle establish sampled/full-catalog metric disagreement [3]. Fixed candidates aid reproducibility without removing that discrepancy.

Three directions remain: recurrent correctness, temporal reliance, and evidence-grounded feedback interpretation.

## Framework

| Layer | Measurement | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness | Padding-invariance error | Implementation validity |
| Temporal behavior | Paired ranks after history edits | In-sample reliance; possible memorization |
| Feedback grounding | Supported/contradicted/unknown evidence | No inferred ownership or mood |
| Selection | Host macro validation HR@10 | Sole model-selection objective |

## Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means more implementation work.

1. **Padding-invariance gate — 3/8/2.** Compare identical histories across padding lengths. Originality: useful family adaptation, but established checking; potential: prevents invalid conclusions, but supplies no preference signal; difficulty: compact checks, but repairs require predictor parity [4].
2. **Paired temporal-reliance adapter — 4/7/5.** Compare matched history edits on training-prefix targets. Originality: integrated controls, but established methods; potential: narrows hypotheses, but in-sample sensitivity cannot establish generalization; difficulty: reuses ModelView, but matching, scoring and uncertainty require care [1–3,5–8].
3. **Evidence-grounded feedback rubric — 5/6/5.** Annotate recent alignment, possible redundancy and identity clarity. Originality: task-specific synthesis, but familiar annotation principles; potential: clarifies feedback, but twenty users limit evidence; difficulty: simple schema, but independent annotation and adjudication require effort.

## Selected idea: Paired temporal-reliance adapter

At 0% progress, retain the feasible diagnostic extension, with padding correctness as its prerequisite. Freeze each category’s single GRU4Rec. Training-prefix findings describe reliance, including possible memorization and perturbation artifacts; they cannot establish causal intent or validation gains [5,8].

```text
verify unchanged-input controls, padding invariance and final readout
sample training prefixes reproducibly; fix targets and candidates
repeat prefix shuffles while preserving the final observed item
delete equal recent/older counts while preserving that final item
separately delete the final item as a recency stress test
record paired ranks, reciprocal ranks, hits and top-10 overlap
average within users; bootstrap users within each category
average four category effects equally in every replicate
```

Preserve both diagnostic methods, measured definitions, existing margin probes and model mode. Report counts, unavailable observations, perturbation randomness and conditional uncertainty. Document candidate eligibility, repeated targets and ties explicitly. Leave the host evaluator unchanged; its sampled validation and simulator full-catalog recommendations answer different questions. Consider architectural interventions only after this diagnostic, selecting exclusively through pinned validation.

idea.description: Extend the family-aware GRU4Rec adapter with padding checks and controlled, paired history perturbations measuring in-sample temporal reliance. Preserve the distinction between earlier-order dependence, recent-context dependence and final-item dependence.
idea.motivation: Existing margin and embedding probes cannot distinguish these mechanisms. Qualitative feedback suggests investigating recent relevance, but does not establish its cause. At initial research progress, a bounded diagnostic is more defensible than introducing an untested architecture. Large perturbation effects may reflect memorization or unrealistic histories, so the revised idea makes no generalization claim.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve all four category routes and exactly one independently trained GRU4Rec checkpoint per category. Use only training histories for these additional diagnostics; training-prefix targets may already have contributed to fitting and must be labeled in-sample. Do not change splits or reserve new training holdouts. Keep seed 42, using a local diagnostic RNG that does not alter training randomness. Select at most four eligible prefix endpoints per training user without replacement; require at least three observed items and a subsequent target. Record selected endpoints and the total eligible and sampled user/prefix counts. Preserve repeated item occurrences and repeated targets.

For each original prefix of length n, set k=max(1,floor((n-1)/4)). Delete either the first k items or the k items immediately preceding the final observation; retain the final observation in both comparisons. Preserve surviving chronological order and left-pad both edited inputs to the same width. Separately remove only the final observation as a recency stress test. Generate five seeded permutations of all preceding nonpadding positions, keeping the final observation, length and item multiset fixed. Permit unchanged permutations and report their frequency; do not selectively redraw them. Average outcomes across permutations before user aggregation.

Construct diagnostic candidates once per original prefix: its target plus 99 uniformly sampled unique real items excluding the original observed prefix and target. Preserve target eligibility even when the target already occurs in the prefix. Skip and count cases with fewer than 99 eligible negatives. Fix candidate identities and order across every perturbation; never regenerate exclusions from an edited history. Use item-ID order and item-ID ascending tie breaking for this explicitly separate diagnostic protocol. Compute target rank, reciprocal rank, HR@10, top-10 Jaccard overlap and paired changes, with rank increases defined as deterioration. This diagnostic candidate policy does not claim to reproduce the host evaluator. Retain the host's existing eligibility, seen-item exclusions, repeated-target handling and tie behavior unchanged; document them only if supplied or verified, otherwise mark them unspecified.

In eval mode, compare unchanged-input repeats, padding variants and unpadded single-sequence predictions. Check final features and candidate logits with atol=1e-6 and rtol=1e-5, recording maximum errors. Read the maximum nonpadding index, never count-1. Skip empty histories. If invariance fails, report the failure and withhold temporal interpretation until corrected. Any recurrent fix must skip padding updates or compact valid sequences, restore B x L feature alignment and update the embedded predictor writer identically. Preserve ModelView.log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items), including B x L x 2 candidate scoring and the loader contract (None, sequence, positive, negative). view.model remains the trained nn.Module.

Retain valid-position margins and embedding geometry, including their score-scale and interpretation limitations. Represent absent valid observations as unavailable rather than zero. Remove unsupported metadata-category breakdowns; do not infer item categories from dataset routing. Use only supplied histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions. Review text, ratings, prices, stores, ownership, compatibility, mood and simulator traits remain unavailable or unknown unless explicitly observed.

Average prefix effects within each user, then weight users equally within each category. Report category results before the equally weighted four-category macro effect. Fix length strata at 3–5, 6–10, 11–20 and 21+ observed items. Define target popularity by training interaction counts, with item-count tertile boundaries fixed before scoring; report boundaries and subgroup counts. Use 1,000 paired user-cluster bootstrap replicates, resampling users within categories and retaining every selected user's matched prefixes and perturbations. Recompute category effects and their equally weighted macro average in every replicate; report percentile 95% intervals. These intervals condition on fitted checkpoints and sampled diagnostic histories; they exclude training randomness, search selection and in-sample bias. Repeated shuffles are not independent users. Predeclare these settings and count diagnostic GPU time against the shared budget.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) embedding both. Store diagnostic specifications and sampled identifiers beneath the trial directory. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Keep execution single-GPU. Do not read other trials or hidden test data, fetch pretrained weights, combine independent predictors or modify the evaluator. Model selection remains the unchanged 200-user/category, 99-unique-negative, evaluation-seed-42 macro validation HR@10. Keep the simulator's twenty training users and full-catalog unseen-item recommendations separate. No improvement is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    previous_mode = view.model.training
    try:
        view.model.eval()
        enter inference_mode()
        metrics = existing_family_compatible_probes(train_loader)
        mark_missing_measurements_unavailable(metrics)
        prefixes = sample_up_to_four_training_prefixes_per_user(local_seed=42)
        controls = compare_unchanged_padding_and_unpadded_execution(prefixes)
        record_controls_and_tolerances(controls, atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-5)
        if controls.fail:
            return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions_with_failure}
        for user, history, target in prefixes:
            candidates = sample_once_from_original_prefix(history, target, negatives=99)
            if insufficient_candidates:
                record_skip(); continue
            k = max(1, floor((len(history)-1)/4))
            variants = {
                'original': history,
                'older_delete': history[k:],
                'recent_delete_keep_final': history[:-k-1] + history[-1:],
                'final_delete': history[:-1],
                'prefix_shuffles': five_seeded_prefix_permutations_keep_final(history)
            }
            for name, edited in variants:
                sequence = compact_then_left_pad(edited)
                features = view.log2feats(sequence)
                final = gather_at_maximum_nonpadding_index(features, sequence)
                scores = view.predict_score(final, candidates)
                record_ranks_hits_reciprocal_ranks_and_top10(
                    user, name, scores, tie_break='item_id_ascending')
        average_shuffle_replicates_then_prefixes_within_users()
        report_category_and_predeclared_length_popularity_strata()
        bootstrap_paired_user_clusters_within_categories(replicates=1000, seed=42)
        recompute_equal_four_category_macro_in_every_replicate()
        return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}
    finally:
        view.model.train(previous_mode)

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    embed measured metrics, definitions, controls, counts and limitations
    request evidence-linked findings and testable single-model hypotheses
    distinguish recency dependence, earlier-order sensitivity and predictive outcomes
    label training-prefix results in-sample and intervals checkpoint-conditional
    prohibit causal-intent, held-out-gain and unsupported-metadata claims

originality.positive: Integrates GRU padding checks, final-item-preserving controls and paired target-ranking diagnostics within the required ModelView contract.
originality.negative: The component techniques are established; this is a careful diagnostic integration rather than a new recommendation algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish implementation artifacts and different temporal dependencies before spending budget on controlled GRU4Rec interventions.
future_potential.negative: In-sample reliance can reflect memorization or distribution shift and may fail to identify any intervention that improves pinned validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses one fitted model and existing scoring interfaces without retraining or adding an independent predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible candidate handling, aligned recurrent outputs, matched perturbations, user weighting and clustered uncertainty require substantial care.

related_work.title: Betello et al.: sequential recommendation perturbation study
contributions: Motivates sensitivity analysis by interaction position.
Introduces Finite Rank-Biased Overlap for finite recommendation lists.
limitations: Training-data interventions differ from fixed-model inference perturbations.
List changes do not establish target-ranking improvement or causal user intent; FRBO is optional here, while Jaccard overlap is specified.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Studies original versus shuffled histories, including GRU4Rec.
Combines accuracy measurements with recommendation-set comparisons.
limitations: Order sensitivity varies across datasets.
Its results do not directly establish the behavior of the proposed final-item-preserving frozen-model diagnostic.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics and reverse model comparisons.
Supports explicitly documenting candidate scope.
limitations: Fixed candidates improve reproducibility without eliminating sampling bias.
Does not justify changing the pinned host evaluator or establish which GRU4Rec intervention will improve it.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Specifies equations showing that zero input need not preserve recurrent state.
Provides an implementation basis for padding-invariance checks.
limitations: Does not demonstrate a padding bug in the supplied baseline.
Correct padding alone does not establish recommendation quality.

related_work.title: Permutation feature importance
contributions: Distinguishes interpretation on training data from held-out generalization.
Supports labeling fitted-history perturbations as in-sample reliance measurements.
limitations: General permutation-importance guidance does not validate a particular sequential-history editing scheme.
Perturbations can create unrealistic inputs and correlated sequence positions complicate attribution.

related_work.title: Robust Training of Sequential Recommender Systems with Missing Input Data
contributions: Explains how missing final observations alter prediction context.
Motivates separating final-item deletion from final-item-preserving edits.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed diagnostic's results on these four datasets.
Performance degradation after deletion alone cannot identify useful longer-range temporal reasoning.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Defines paired resampling that preserves correspondence between compared observations.
Supports preserving original-versus-perturbed pairing during uncertainty estimation.
limitations: Paired array resampling alone does not implement user-cluster resampling; users must explicitly be the resampling units.
Bootstrap intervals do not remove in-sample bias or account automatically for checkpoint and search uncertainty.

related_work.title: Ji et al.: temporal leakage and evaluation in sequential recommendation
contributions: Documents the importance of temporal leakage and evaluation protocol in sequential recommendation.
Supports preserving fixed splits and separating diagnostic observations from held-out claims.
limitations: Does not demonstrate leakage in this supplied benchmark.
Does not establish that the proposed perturbation measurements predict validation improvement.

related_work.title: An Analysis of Sequential Recommendation Datasets
contributions: Compares chronological and shuffled training histories while retaining evaluation targets.
Provides context for investigating whether ordering contributes predictive information.
limitations: Retraining on shuffled histories differs from editing inputs to a frozen model.
Its findings cannot be transferred directly to final-item-preserving inference perturbations.

related_work.title: Cluster-bootstrap research
contributions: Supports resampling clusters to preserve dependence among observations belonging to the same unit.
Motivates retaining each user's matched prefixes together during resampling.
limitations: Cluster-bootstrap principles do not determine the appropriate scientific estimand; equal-user weighting must be specified separately.
Resampling observed users does not account for training randomness or correct training-set optimism.
